title: Alert when a protocol file stops being served
statement: The files crawlers read to learn how to treat the site, including robots.txt, the sitemap index, any feed, and any verification resource, are fetched on a schedule from the production host, and a non-success response raises an alert.
rationale: An unavailable robots.txt is not treated as an absent one, so a deployment that stops serving it changes how the whole site is crawled without changing any page, and nothing on the site looks broken.
implementation: Fetch each file from the public host rather than from inside the network, so an edge rule that blocks it is visible to the check. Assert on status and on a shape the file must have, since a challenge page can return a success status.

verification.method: Request each protocol file from the production host on schedule and assert both a success status and a body that parses as the format the file claims.

title: Alert on an unplanned change to an indexing directive
statement: The exclusion directives and canonical values served by a set of representative routes are recorded, compared after each deployment, and any difference nobody asked for raises an alert before the next deployment lands on top of it.
rationale: A directive that excludes a page from the index produces no error and no visible defect, so an accidental one persists until traffic falls far enough for someone to investigate weeks later.
implementation: Pick routes covering each template rather than a fixed list of popular pages, store the recorded values as a baseline, and require an explicit baseline update so a change has to be acknowledged to be accepted.

verification.method: Capture served directives and canonical values across the representative routes, diff against the stored baseline, and report differences with no corresponding baseline update.

caution: The cited documentation specifies what the directives do, not that they should be monitored for drift, so the monitoring requirement is this registry's inference and the record is tier B.

sources.title: Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications

title: Define the rollback condition before a discoverability change ships
statement: A change to redirects, canonical values, exclusion directives, sitemap behaviour, or address structure is accompanied, before it ships, by the signal that would mean it went wrong and the steps that would undo it.
rationale: These changes take effect gradually and are noticed through falling traffic rather than an error, so a decision about when to revert made after the decline has begun is made while under pressure and short of information.
implementation: Write the reverting steps as part of preparing the change, and confirm they work on a copy first, since a redirect map or a directive change is frequently easier to apply than to withdraw.

verification.method: Confirm each shipped high-impact change has a recorded reverting procedure and a named signal, and that the procedure was exercised somewhere before shipping.

caution: This is a practice this project imposes on itself rather than a platform behaviour, so it carries no external citation. How long to wait before reverting depends on the site's own traffic pattern and is not fixed here.

title: Record the command and output behind every verification claim
statement: A requirement reported as verified names what was run, what it returned, and what the run could not reach, and no requirement is reported as verified on the strength of a file having been edited.
rationale: A report that states conclusions without the observations behind them cannot be checked by whoever reads it, so it has to be either believed or redone, and both defeat the point of having run it.
implementation: Capture the invocation and its output as the verification result rather than writing a summary from memory afterwards, and state the limits of the run alongside it where something was unreachable.

verification.method: Inspect the generated report and confirm every verified requirement carries a recorded invocation and its output, rejecting entries whose only evidence is a file modification.

caution: This governs how this process reports on itself and asserts nothing about any platform, so it needs no citation. It is the rule that makes every other verification method in this registry meaningful rather than decorative.

title: Capture the prior state before changing a search-critical output
statement: Before a change to a title, a canonical value, a directive, a redirect, or a structured description, the current served value is recorded, so the change can be described as a difference rather than asserted as an improvement.
rationale: Without the prior value there is nothing to compare against, so a change cannot be shown to have done what was intended and a regression cannot be distinguished from the state that was already there.
implementation: Snapshot the affected routes from the production host first, keep the snapshot with the change, and diff against it afterwards rather than against what the source now says.

verification.method: Confirm a stored snapshot predating each change exists for the routes it touched, and that the reported difference was computed against that snapshot.

caution: Comparing against a prior snapshot shows what changed on the site. It shows nothing about how any platform responded to the change, and no report may read one as the other.

title: Close each applicable requirement with evidence or a stated blocker
statement: Every requirement the site profile activates ends the run in a recorded state, either satisfied with evidence, not applicable with the reason, blocked with what is missing, or uncertain with what would settle it, and none is left silently unaddressed.
rationale: An unmentioned requirement is indistinguishable from a satisfied one in a report, which is how a partial audit comes to read as a complete one.
implementation: Enumerate the activated set first and reconcile the report against it at the end, so a requirement that was never examined appears as uncertain rather than vanishing from the output.

verification.method: Compare the activated requirement set against the reported outcomes and fail the run where any activated requirement has no recorded state.

caution: Uncertain is a legitimate outcome and is preferred to a guess, because a requirement marked uncertain invites the evidence that would settle it while a wrongly satisfied one closes the question.
